title: Prawn Masala
subtitle: Quick spiced prawns in a tomato and cream sauce
excerpt: Prawn masala is fast, weeknight-friendly Indian cooking at its best. Raw prawns cook in under 5 minutes once the sauce is ready, so most of the effort is in building the base. The cream rounds the sauce without making it heavy.
sourceNotes: Prawn masala is common across coastal India, from Goa to Kerala to Bengal. Each region uses different spice combinations and levels of heat. This version draws on the broader North Indian masala style, which uses tomatoes and cream.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato base can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept refrigerated. Add the prawns just before serving.

content.text: Raw prawns give a far better result than pre-cooked. If using frozen raw prawns, thaw them completely and pat them dry before adding to the pan -- excess water will cause the sauce to split and turn watery.

items.prepNote: peeled and deveined, tails on or off

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the turmeric, cumin, and coriander. Stir for 1 minute to cook the spices into the oil.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Add salt. Cook on medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the prawns. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until they are pink and just cooked through. Do not overcook.
Pour in the cream and stir through. Add the garam masala. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve at once with rice or naan.

items.cause: Overcooked -- they need only 3 to 4 minutes
items.fix: Remove them from the sauce the moment they curl and turn pink

items.cause: The tinned tomatoes need longer cooking to lose their raw edge
items.fix: Cook the tomato sauce for 2 extra minutes before adding the cream

items.cause: The cream was added when the pan was too hot
items.fix: Take the pan off the heat for 30 seconds before stirring in the cream

content.text: Prawns and the sea have shaped India's coastal cooking for thousands of years. This style of tomato-based masala with cream is particularly common in restaurant cooking across the UK and North America. The freshness of the prawn is the star -- everything else is there to support it.
